So after seeing it a bit dead I figured we could use a discussion post. Some of my favorites include: Hellboy and his extended universe. I've not read a Hellboy book I didn't enjoy, the BPRD is great, and so is Lobster Johnson. Haven't read Abe Sapiens solo series or Witchfinder yet though.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles. The new IDW run is great if you haven't got a chance to read it yet. Just like the old school turtles, and even written by one of the creators, Kevin Eastman! Perfect mix of goofy and drama. IDW has also recently released a collection including the first two trades and the miniseries here on Amazon.
To liven the place up let's have a discussion! What are some of your favorite comics? Runs, characters etc.
I'm a big fan of Tank Girl, Ultimate Avengers, East of West, Transmetropolitan and the Sandman series.
How is Sandman? It's always looked interesting but that art is a little harsh, but I can overlook it if the story is good enough. That's how I powered through Hellblazer.

They actually switch artists up a couple different times. The sketch-like art at the beginning adds to the "dreamlike" quality of the first volume, in my opinion.

It's definitely worth checking out. I went into it only knowing Neil Gaiman wrote it, and I was hooked. I couldn't stop. I don't know how someone could write a comic book for 60+ issues and maintain continuity and quality, but Sandman is a perfect example of that. It's very dark, as well (somewhat like watchmen). Not exactly typical superhero fare, although since it's set in the DC universe, it has some cameos.

Big fan of Y: The Last Man, and Hickman's FF run. Actually pretty much anything by Hickman. Also Nextwave Agents of HATE is an amazing little Marvel series.

I'm currently reading the trades of Adventure Time and loving it as well. Really captures the tone of the series while doing its own thing and doing it well.

I've only recently been reading comics but my favorites and monthly "I can't wait!" series have to be Annihilator, C.O.W.L. and Death Vigil.

Annihilator is probably my favorite out of the three right now. The concept and story are so crazy that I love it. Morrison does an excellent job of creating these characters and feeling the eccentricity through the pages!

C.O.W.L. was the first series I chose to read on my own that didn't come recommended. The art by Rod Reis really lends to the tone of the 50s tough and gritty crime scene. The writing is also fantastic with the pair, Alec Siegel and Kyle Higgins. The original story was supposed to start right off the bat, but both Alec and Kyle decided to delve into the back story a bit. This led to the series having a huge amount of involvement in each character's story that while you read it, you can almost imagine and feel the emotion of each character.

Death Vigil is probably my most fun comic to ready. It started out as a light hearted story, but is quickly becoming a dark monstrosity of chaos and panic. Stjepan does an amazing job of illustrating his character's emotion and also through his writing.

I have way more, but 3 is probably enough :)

Recent series I've read and enjoyed: Saga, Sex Criminals, Fraction & Aja's run on Hawkeye, Invincible

Older series that I recommend to anyone who can handle them: Transmetropolitian, Preacher, Y: The Last Man, The Boys, Sandman, Mage: The Hero Discovered and Mage: The Hero Defined... well, pretty much anything by Warren Ellis, Garth Ennis, Matt Wagner, and Neil Gaiman. :)

I thought that would be a good idea. Have a list of areas that a subverse could fall into, and have a person select an area when they're creating one. Like Culture, Technology, and so on. I don't think this is very useful right now, but I think it could be useful once it expands and subverses get used for more specific things, like ones for particular video games franchises instead of just video games in general.

So you could have, for example, a /v/Megaten and that could be found under the category Video Games or Entertainment, if you wanted to be less specific.

This would, I think, make it easier for people to get interested in new things in an area they already like. You can search for something you're looking for specifically, yeah, but if you want to see what else is going on in that area, this could be a decent way to do it, I believe.
